data.name: Iron Warriors: T-72 Tank Command
data.detailed_description:
O exército mecanizado mais devastador que alguma vez participou numa batalha é trazido de novo à vida em Iron Warriors: T72-Tank Command. Este simulador épico de combates permite que o jogador comande um pelotão completo de tanques e TODAS as unidades de suporte associadas, ou assumir o papel de QUALQUER um dos ocupantes de um tanque!

O realismo da física e do motor 3D cria ambientes de jogo onde a táctica armada real se torna a única forma de sobreviver nas batalhas modernas dos dias de hoje!

  • Pode controlar três dos tanques mais devastadores de sempre construídos na Rússia: o T–34-85, o T-55A e o T-72B!

  • Utilize estes monstros mecanizados ao longo de 18 campanhas, 2 missões de treino, 5 missões de jogador individual e 3 missões multi-jogador (LAN).

  • Aperfeiçoe o seu tanque e os membros da sua equipa e em breve irá comandar outras unidades que rodeiam o seu pelotão mecanizado.

  • O suporte multi-jogador em cooperação permite que os utilizadores formem equipas num tanque e joguem em diferentes posições dentro do mesmo tanque!

  • Entre na batalha em alguns dos mapas de terreno mais realistas de sempre, condições atmosféricas reais, terrenos destrutíveis e modelos detalhados.

  • Os modelos balísticos têm em conta: vento, bombas, características aerodinâmicas de voo, desgaste de cartuchos e queda!

  • Potentes editores de missões, mapas e estruturas incluídos; possibilidade de modificar conteúdo existente ou criar o seu próprio conteúdo.

Iron Warriors is a tank simulation game. The user engages in tank battles with the enemy. 
There is blood and violence and was rated MATURE by the ESRB

reviews.review:
Iron Warriors: T-72 Tank Command is an old-school armored warfare simulator built around the idea that operating a tank should involve much more than pointing a cannon at an enemy and firing. Developed by Crazy House and published by Strategy First, it approaches tank combat with an emphasis on simulation, crew responsibilities, ballistics, and tactical positioning. Its age is immediately apparent in its presentation and interface, but beneath those dated elements is a surprisingly ambitious military simulation aimed at players who enjoy learning how armored vehicles function rather than simply using them as oversized weapons.

One of its strongest qualities is the selection of playable Soviet-designed tanks. The T-34-85, T-55A, and T-72B represent different generations of armored warfare, allowing the game to explore machines with noticeably different capabilities. Players can take control of individual crew positions rather than having every function conveniently condensed into a standard action-game control scheme. Driving, observing the battlefield, locating targets, and operating the weapons all contribute to the experience. This creates a steep learning curve, but understanding these systems is also where much of the satisfaction comes from.

Gunnery is considerably more sophisticated than the game's dated appearance might suggest. Shell behavior is influenced by factors such as ammunition characteristics, wind, barrel condition, and other ballistic considerations. Engagements consequently reward preparation and accuracy rather than frantic shooting. Spotting an enemy first, estimating the situation, selecting appropriate ammunition, and finding a strong firing position can determine the outcome before the first shell leaves the barrel. Tank armor provides protection, but reckless exposure is still dangerous, making terrain and situational awareness essential parts of survival.

There is also more content here than a simple collection of tank battles. The campaign contains 18 scenarios alongside training missions and additional standalone missions. As the experience develops, the player can become responsible for more than one vehicle and command supporting elements of a mechanized platoon. This gives battles an interesting combination of first-person vehicle simulation and broader tactical decision-making. Ordering other units while simultaneously worrying about the position and condition of your own tank can be demanding, yet it helps communicate the complexity of mechanized combat.

The environments support this tactical approach through large battlefields where elevation, cover, visibility, and positioning matter. Weather effects and destructible terrain add additional atmosphere, while the vehicle models communicate the game's focus on military hardware. Visually, there is no escaping the fact that this is a product of an earlier generation. Terrain can look sparse, effects are basic by contemporary standards, and animations lack modern refinement. Nevertheless, visual spectacle was never the main objective. The environments primarily exist to provide functional spaces for armored engagements, and they accomplish that purpose reasonably well.

Another impressive feature is the inclusion of editing tools. Players can work with missions, maps, and structures, offering opportunities to experiment beyond the supplied scenarios. Multiplayer was also designed with unusually ambitious ideas, including cooperative play where several people could occupy different crew positions within a single tank. LAN missions and competitive options further broadened the original package. These multiplayer features should now be considered legacy functionality because of the game's age, so the single-player component remains the most dependable attraction for someone approaching it today.

Its biggest weaknesses are closely connected to its age and simulation-heavy philosophy. The interface can feel cumbersome, controls require patience, and artificial intelligence does not always behave convincingly. Modern players accustomed to streamlined tutorials and highly polished control schemes may find the opening hours particularly difficult. Technical compatibility can also require more patience than with contemporary releases because the game originates from the Windows XP and DirectX 9 period. The extremely modest original hardware requirements make performance demands trivial for modern PCs, but old software can introduce compatibility issues unrelated to raw processing power.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially listed as Unknown rather than Steam Deck Verified or Playable. Because this is an older Windows game built around traditional PC controls, players should not assume a seamless handheld experience. Proton may allow experimentation, but controls, interface readability, launcher behavior, or other legacy compatibility issues could require manual configuration. Anyone purchasing specifically for Steam Deck use should therefore regard support as unverified rather than guaranteed.

Iron Warriors: T-72 Tank Command ultimately succeeds because it knows exactly what kind of experience it wants to provide. It is not a polished modern tank action game and makes few concessions to players seeking immediate accessibility. Instead, it offers methodical armored warfare where understanding your vehicle, selecting positions carefully, managing crew functions, and thinking tactically are central to success. Its presentation and usability have aged considerably, but its combination of detailed tank operation, ballistic simulation, tactical command, substantial campaign content, and editing tools still gives it character. For military simulation enthusiasts willing to work around its rough edges, there remains an engaging and unusually focused armored warfare experience here.

Rating: 7/10
